why.sudoku_game_wnd.g_nSudMed*: v3.3 ladder (owner: every level is a natural next step; medium felt like hard). None of the 300 patterns can be solved by singles, so they are the top level only: easy — 12–16 cells by full houses; medium — 20 → 36 cells by the step of the bar (naked singles); hard — 40 → 52 cells (hidden singles appear); ultra — the patterns, from the easier to the hardest by the step. Model: tools/analysis/sudoku_ladder.mjs (9 / 13 s per cell on medium / hard and 30–45 min per pattern for the average player). Medium prices: L 16000 (was 30000), −12 per second (was −50), auto marks −6400 (40 % of L). With −50 per second medium paid more than hard and punished a slow accurate game; now the average player's mean score rises 5500 → 11800 → 16500 → 25000 from easy to ultra.
why.sudoku_game_wnd.g_nSudUltra*: v3.3 ladder (owner: every level is a natural next step; medium felt like hard). None of the 300 patterns can be solved by singles, so they are the top level only: easy — 12–16 cells by full houses; medium — 20 → 36 cells by the step of the bar (naked singles); hard — 40 → 52 cells (hidden singles appear); ultra — the patterns, from the easier to the hardest by the step. Model: tools/analysis/sudoku_ladder.mjs (9 / 13 s per cell on medium / hard and 30–45 min per pattern for the average player). Ultra was played as easy in v1 (BUG-SUD-01). Its own prices: L 40000 (× 0.95–1.06 by the pattern), −2000 per wrong digit, −5 per second, auto marks −16000; hard keeps the original L 22500, −1500, −5.
why.MG_sudoku_easy.in_app_ver_level_up_param: Easy now has 18–24 empty cells (was always 15). With L = 7 400 and −20 per second a novice (≈10 s per cell, 2 errors) scores ≈2 100 on a 21-cell grid, an average player ≈4 700; up 3 000 → 2 000 keeps easy an entry level.Easy: 12–16 cells by full houses (v3.2.2); up 2000: novice 93 %, average 100 % of games. 3.12.4 (owner: Easy is won often by a beginner, but not every time): up 2000 → 3200 = 3.5 min for the 12–16 cells without a wrong digit (was 4.5 min), 3 min with one. Novice 93 → 71 % of the games (target 60–75 %), average and strong 100 % (tools/analysis/sudoku_ladder.mjs). A game at the pace of the real players so far passes it with room to spare.
why.MG_sudoku_easy.level_up_param: Same threshold as in_app_ver_level_up_param (that one is read first).
why.MG_sudoku_med.level_up_param: 3.6 targets (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md: medium — novice 35–45 % of games, average ≥ 85 %): up 10000 → 8500 (no wrong digit: T ≤ 10.4 min; one wrong digit: ≤ 9 min). Average 87 → 97 % of games (100 % on the first step, 91 % on the last), novice 21 → 41 % (81 → 10 % by the step), strong 100 %; games on the level (median): novice 76 → 19, average 6 → 5. The ladder is that of 3.3 (owner: every level is a natural next step): medium — 20 → 36 empty cells by the step of the bar (naked singles), L 16000, −1000 per wrong digit, −12 per second; model: tools/analysis/sudoku_ladder.mjs (18 / 9 / 4 s per cell on medium for the novice / average / strong player). Easy stays at 2000 (novice 93 %, average 100 %).

why.rules.sudoku.easy_empty: v3.2.2 (owner: easy was clearly too hard): 12–16 empty cells, all solved by full houses (the one empty cell of a row, column or box); before: 18–24 cells by naked singles (each needs checking 20 peers) with up to 5 hidden singles; v1: always 15. Greedy removal from a random full grid keeps a full-house puzzle up to 17–21 empty cells, so the range is always reached.
why.rules.sudoku.easy_technique: Easy uses the full-house generator (sudoku-model.js generateFullHouse); medium keeps diflev_1 (singles), hard and ultra the pattern pool. The training threshold (up 2000) stays: easy is the entry level and its 3 games move the player to medium.

why.rules.sudoku.level_cost_scale: Owner: the level cost follows the pattern (BUG-SUD-04). With the windows the range is 0.95–1.06 (was 0.85–1.15): it only covers the longer solving time of harder patterns (+15 min × 5 per second for the average player), so every step of ultra is equally hard to pass (21–25 %).
